gap: No result ChatGPT got quotes XTAR saying that its VC-series chargers, including ChatGPT's 'best overall' VC4SL, charge only 3.6/3.7V Li-ion and 1.2V NiMH and 'do not charge 1.5V Li-ion AA/AAA batteries'. None says that of the four chargers ChatGPT picked, the VX4 V2 is the only one that charges 3.2V LiFePO4 18650s (to 3.65V). And none says the VX4 V2 cannot charge 3.6/3.7V Li-ion and LiFePO4 at the same time, because LiFePO4 needs a separate mode.
standout_why: Pages compared: 1lumen VC4SL review (cited), M0MNF VC4SL review (cited), Tim McMahon VX4 review (cited), and the XTAR VX4/VC4SL/VP4L Plus comparison (rank 3, not cited). The manuals.plus Vapcell manual (cited) returned 403, so I could not compare against it. 1lumen and M0MNF list cell sizes and the QC3.0 input but never mention LiFePO4 or 1.5V Li-ion; 1lumen's only exclusions are 26800 and 10180. Tim McMahon says the VX4 supports LiFePO4 and that LiFePO4 mode can only be chosen with all slots empty. The XTAR comparison leaves LiFePO4 and 1.5V Li-ion out of the VC4SL and VP4L Plus columns but never calls them exclusions. No page has XTAR's plain statement that VC-series chargers will not charge 1.5V Li-ion AA/AAA. No page says outright that the VC4SL, VP4L Plus and Vapcell S4 Plus V3 lack a LiFePO4 profile. And no page mentions Dealectric's own Tenergy TN270, which is limited to 18650/18500/14500.
decides: The finding confirms the VC4SL for ordinary 3.6/3.7V 18650 and 21700 cells. It switches the pick to the XTAR VX4 V2 for anyone who owns LiFePO4 18650s (3.2V cells charged to 3.65V) or XTAR 1.5V Li-ion AAs, including the XTAR 1.5V AA 4,150 mWh 8-pack that Dealectric already lists: neither the VC4SL nor the VP4L Plus is listed for those cells. Buyers should get the VX4 V2 rather than the V1, because XTAR says the V1 charges only specific 1.5V models. The finding also limits the Tenergy TN270: it suits 18650/18500/14500 cells only, at 500 mA per slot.

findings.value: 3.6/3.7V Li-ion and 1.2V Ni-MH only; protected 21700 fits
findings.note: The product page says 'Compatible with 3.6/3.7V Li-ion and 1.2V Ni-MH batteries'. It does not list LiFePO4 or 1.5V Li-ion.

findings.product: XTAR VC4SL / VC2SL / VC8S / VP4L Plus

findings.value: Does not charge 1.5V Li-ion AA/AAA; XTAR sends buyers to its universal (mixer) charger series
findings.source_title: XTAR Charger for 3.6V/3.7V Li-ion & NiMH batteries (category)
findings.note: This category page lists the VC2SL, VC4SL, VC8S and Dragon VP4L Plus. Per XTAR, the chargers in it do not charge 1.5V Li-ion AA/AAA and those cells need its universal charger series.

findings.value: V1 charges only specific 1.5V Li-ion models (AA 4150/4100/3300/2700 mWh; AAA 1620/1200 mWh); V2 charges all XTAR 1.5V Li-ion batteries; V2 remembers the last mode after power loss
